features.name: Array text conversion
features.description: Ordinary array joining and text conversion execute independently in JS and collecting zero-import WASM, with the selected cycle error and original evaluation order.

scenarios.given: an empty array and a sparse four-position array
scenarios.when: both arrays are joined with default separators
scenarios.then: empty text and exactly three separators are returned
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-array))) (put a :length 4) (js-array (js-call (js-array) :join) (js-call a :join))))

scenarios.given: negative zero, NaN, infinity, the smallest subnormal and Unicode text
scenarios.when: the values are joined with a vertical bar
scenarios.then: their exact existing JS text is retained
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-call (js-array -0.0 (/ 0 0) (/ 1 0) 5e-324 "中😀") :join "|"))

scenarios.given: two positions refer to the same noncircular child
scenarios.when: the parent is joined
scenarios.then: both child occurrences are preserved
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((child (js-array "x"))) (js-call (js-array child child) :join "|")))

scenarios.given: separator conversion appends an array item
scenarios.when: join converts that separator
scenarios.then: the original length is used and the append remains observable
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((a (js-array "x")) (sep (js-object :toString (lambda () (js-call a :push "late") "|")))) (let ((out (js-call a :join sep))) (js-array out (js-length a)))))

scenarios.given: the first element conversion changes the second element
scenarios.when: join reads elements in order
scenarios.then: the later read observes the changed value
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-array nil "old"))) (put a 0 (js-object :toString (lambda () (put a 1 "changed") "first"))) (js-call a :join "|")))

scenarios.given: toString returns an object and valueOf returns a number
scenarios.when: the containing array is joined
scenarios.then: callbacks run once in string-hint order and the number becomes text
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((trace (js-array)) (item (js-object :toString (lambda () (js-call trace :push "to") (js-object)) :valueOf (lambda () (js-call trace :push "value") 7))) (out (js-call (js-array item) :join))) (js-array out (js-call trace :join ">"))))

scenarios.given: an own join function is replaced while evaluating an argument
scenarios.when: the original method call completes
scenarios.then: the previously captured function is called
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-array "x"))) (put a :join (lambda (&rest ignored) "captured")) (js-call a :join (progn (put a :join (lambda () "replacement")) "|"))))

scenarios.given: toString has an ignored argument that installs an own join
scenarios.when: toString executes after the argument
scenarios.then: the newly installed join is observed
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-array "x"))) (js-call a :toString (put a :join (lambda () "changed")))))

scenarios.given: an own join returns a source object
scenarios.when: array toString calls that join
scenarios.then: the exact original object is returned
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-array)) (answer (js-object))) (put a :join (lambda () answer)) (eq (js-call a :toString) answer)))

scenarios.given: an array item points to the containing array
scenarios.when: join is attempted and the item is then replaced
scenarios.then: both targets report ELI-RT0009 and the same array can be joined afterwards
scenarios.source: (defvar values (js-array "苹果" nil "香蕉")) (defun run () (put values 1 values) (js-call values :join "、")) (defun recover () (put values 1 "梨") (js-call values :join "、"))

scenarios.given: two arrays refer back to each other
scenarios.when: array toString is attempted and the first edge is replaced
scenarios.then: both targets report the cycle error and release the active conversion state
scenarios.source: (defvar values (js-array nil)) (defvar other (js-array values)) (defun run () (put values 0 other) (js-call values :toString)) (defun recover () (put values 0 "safe") (js-call values :toString))

features.name: Represented type and null queries
features.description: Type queries inspect represented bindings without string conversion, retain lexical capture and member failure, and keep the current four null-predicate meanings. Unsupported capabilities remain explicit.

scenarios.given: values include nil, undefined, Boolean, Number, String, Array and a function
scenarios.when: typeof queries run inside the compiled module
scenarios.then: the exact seven JS labels are returned
scenarios.source: (defun label (value) (js* "typeof value")) (defun run () (js-array (label nil) (label undefined) (label false) (label -0.0) (label "中😀") (label (js-array)) (label label)))

scenarios.given: a closure captures an object whose member is later changed
scenarios.when: the captured member type is queried
scenarios.then: the later undefined value is observed
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((value (js-object :item 7)) (f (lambda () (js* "typeof value.item")))) (put value :item undefined) (funcall f)))

scenarios.given: a represented object has no requested member
scenarios.when: its member type is queried
scenarios.then: undefined is returned without stringifying the object
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((trace (js-object :calls 0)) (value (js-object :toString (lambda () (put trace :calls 1) "wrong")))) (js-array (js* "typeof value.item") (get trace :calls))))

scenarios.given: the operand is undefined and one expression counts its own evaluation
scenarios.when: nil, undefined and null predicates are applied
scenarios.then: their existing meanings remain distinct and the effect runs once
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((value undefined) (trace (js-object :calls 0))) (js-array (nil? value) (undefined? value) (null value) (nullish? value) (null (progn (put trace :calls (1+ (get trace :calls))) value)) (get trace :calls))))

scenarios.given: the operand is nil
scenarios.when: all four null predicates are applied
scenarios.then: nil is not confused with undefined
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-array (nil? nil) (undefined? nil) (null nil) (nullish? nil)))

scenarios.given: the represented receiver is nil
scenarios.when: a member type is queried
scenarios.then: member access fails instead of being mislabeled undefined
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((value nil)) (js* "typeof value.item")))

scenarios.given: raw JS refers to an unrepresented ambient name
scenarios.when: the module is compiled for managed WASM
scenarios.then: source-bound ELI-B0001 refuses the unsupported capability
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js* "typeof eliscriptUnrepresentedGlobal"))

scenarios.given: an array contains an object with an own dotted property name
scenarios.when: numeric, quoted and negative zero member paths are queried
scenarios.then: all three paths report the exact value type
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((value (js-array (js-object :item 7 :a.b "中😀")))) (js-array (js* "typeof value [ -0 ] . item") (js* "typeof value[0][\"a.b\"]") (js* "typeof value[1]"))))

scenarios.given: a closure captures an array whose element changes
scenarios.when: the closure queries the new element through its captured binding
scenarios.then: the changed Boolean type is observed
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((value-name (js-array (js-object :item 7))) (f (lambda () (js* "typeof value_name[0].item")))) (put value-name 0 (js-object :item false)) (funcall f)))

scenarios.given: an empty array has no first element
scenarios.when: a query accesses a member of that missing element
scenarios.then: the intermediate access fails instead of returning undefined
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((value (js-array))) (js* "typeof value[0].item")))

scenarios.given: a valid JS query uses a computed member key
scenarios.when: the current experimental managed target compiles it
scenarios.then: the unsupported computed key is explicitly refused
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((value (js-array 7)) (key 0)) (js* "typeof value[key]")))

scenarios.given: an operand counts its own evaluation and returns undefined
scenarios.when: the existing value-type intrinsic queries it
scenarios.then: undefined is returned and the count is one
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((trace (js-object :calls 0))) (js-array (value-type (progn (put trace :calls (1+ (get trace :calls))) undefined)) (get trace :calls))))

scenarios.given: objects contain an own language brand or inherit it from a prototype
scenarios.when: value-type and raw typeof inspect them
scenarios.then: only own recognized data brands affect value-type and raw typeof stays object
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((value (js-object :kind "eliscript/keyword")) (child (js-object))) (put child :__proto__ value) (js-array (value-type nil) (value-type value) (js* "typeof value") (value-type child))))

features.name: Text formatting and decomposition
features.description: Pure WASM mappings, exact numeric text, UTF16 padding, replacement and splitting retain source conversions and failures

scenarios.given: mixed scripts, a contextual sigma and a lone UTF16 surrogate
scenarios.when: upper and lower casing run
scenarios.then: full Unicode mappings preserve expansion, context and lone code units
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-array (js-call "ßﬃ😀" :toUpperCase) (js-call "AΣ́" :toLowerCase) (js-call "\ud800A" :toLowerCase)))

scenarios.given: astral fillers and fractional target lengths
scenarios.when: start and end padding run
scenarios.then: padding truncates by UTF16 code unit and converts the target length
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-array (js-call "x" :padStart 4.9 "😀") (js-call "x" :padEnd 4.9 "😀")))

scenarios.given: an exact fractional Number and radix 16
scenarios.when: the Number is converted then cased and padded
scenarios.then: the full ordinary method chain yields the exact text
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-call (js-call (js-call 255.5 :toString 16) :toUpperCase) :padStart 6 "0"))

scenarios.given: two matches and a callback using offsets and the original string
scenarios.when: every match is replaced
scenarios.then: both callbacks receive original UTF16 offsets and input
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-call "a😀a" :replaceAll "a" (lambda (match index original) (str match ":" index ":" original))))

scenarios.given: effectful numeric and separator conversion hooks with a zero limit
scenarios.when: literal split runs
scenarios.then: numeric conversion precedes text conversion even for an empty result
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((trace (js-array)) (n (js-object :valueOf (lambda () (js-call trace :push "limit") 0))) (s (js-object :toString (lambda () (js-call trace :push "separator") "/")))) (js-array (js-call "a/b" :split s n) (js-call trace :join ">"))))

scenarios.given: a separator with an optional capture
scenarios.when: the capture does not participate in a split match
scenarios.then: undefined is an owned element and is distinct from a hole
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((parts (js-call "b" :split (js* "/(a)?b/")))) (js-array (js-length parts) (object-has? parts 1) (js* "typeof parts[1]"))))

scenarios.given: a radix below two and a subsequent valid conversion
scenarios.when: Number.toString validates its radix
scenarios.then: a RangeError is raised without contaminating later calls
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-call 7 :toString 1)) (defun recover () (js-call 255 :toString 16))

features.name: Stable array sorting
features.description: Stable in-place and copying sorts retain exact values, sparse ownership, source identity, callback evaluation order and recovery in collecting zero-import WASM

scenarios.given: a sparse array containing text, undefined and holes
scenarios.when: default sort orders present entries
scenarios.then: the receiver identity is retained, defined text precedes owned undefined, and remaining holes stay absent
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-array))) (put a :length 6) (put a 1 "b") (put a 3 undefined) (put a 5 "a") (let ((out (js-call a :sort))) (js-array (eq out a) (get a 0) (get a 1) (object-has? a 2) (js* "typeof a[2]") (object-has? a 3) (js-length a)))))

scenarios.given: four records with repeated comparison keys
scenarios.when: a source closure orders them by key
scenarios.then: records with equal keys retain their original relative order
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-array (js-object :key 2 :id "a") (js-object :key 1 :id "b") (js-object :key 2 :id "c") (js-object :key 1 :id "d")))) (js-call (js-call a :sort (lambda (a b) (- (get a :key) (get b :key)))) :map (lambda (item) (get item :id)))))

scenarios.given: a source comparator returning NaN for every pair
scenarios.when: sort compares the array
scenarios.then: every comparison is a tie and the original order is preserved
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-call (js-array "c" "a" "b") :sort (lambda (a b) (/ 0 0))))

scenarios.given: an own sort method and arguments with replacement side effects
scenarios.when: the method is captured before all arguments execute
scenarios.then: the captured method runs once and ignored extra arguments still execute
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-array)) (trace (js-object :calls 0))) (put a :sort (lambda (x &rest extras) (js-array x (js-length extras)))) (js-array (js-call a :sort (progn (put a :sort (lambda () "wrong")) "first") (progn (put trace :calls 1) "extra")) (get trace :calls))))

scenarios.given: a sparse source with an owned undefined entry
scenarios.when: toSorted orders a copied snapshot
scenarios.then: the result is distinct and dense while source holes and original values remain unchanged
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-array))) (put a :length 5) (put a 1 "b") (put a 3 undefined) (put a 4 "a") (let ((out (js-call a :toSorted))) (js-array (eq a out) (get out 0) (get out 1) (object-has? out 2) (object-has? out 3) (object-has? out 4) (object-has? a 0) (get a 1) (js-length a)))))

scenarios.given: a copying comparator that overwrites the original source
scenarios.when: toSorted finishes sorting its collected snapshot
scenarios.then: the sorted output and explicit source mutation are separately observable
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((a (js-array 3 1 2)) (out (js-call a :toSorted (lambda (x y) (put a 0 99) (- x y))))) (js-array out a)))

scenarios.given: an empty receiver and a noncallable comparator
scenarios.when: sort validates the comparator before sorting
scenarios.then: a TypeError is reported and a subsequent valid invocation succeeds
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-call (js-array) :sort false)) (defun recover () (js-call (js-array 3 1 2) :sort (lambda (a b) (- a b))))

scenarios.given: an empty copying receiver and a noncallable comparator
scenarios.when: toSorted validates its comparator
scenarios.then: a TypeError is reported without leaking roots and the next copy succeeds
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-call (js-array) :toSorted false)) (defun recover () (js-call (js-array 3 1 2) :toSorted (lambda (a b) (- a b))))

features.name: Integer rounding
features.description: Math round floor ceil and trunc retain exact IEEE boundaries, signed zero and ordinary number conversion in collecting zero-import WASM.

scenarios.given: values immediately below and at one half and a negative half
scenarios.when: Math.round chooses the nearest integer
scenarios.then: ties go toward positive infinity and a negative result of zero retains its sign
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-array (Math/round 0.49999999999999994) (Math/round 0.5) (Math/round -1.5) (= (/ 1 (Math/round -0.5)) (- (/ 1 0)))))

scenarios.given: negative fractional values and the smallest negative subnormal
scenarios.when: floor ceil and trunc apply their distinct integer directions
scenarios.then: the exact integers and the negative zero from ceil are retained
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-array (Math/floor -1.5) (Math/ceil -1.5) (Math/trunc -1.5) (= (/ 1 (Math/ceil -5e-324)) (- (/ 1 0)))))

scenarios.given: extra argument effects and an object whose valueOf returns another object
scenarios.when: Math.round converts the first argument
scenarios.then: all arguments finish before valueOf then toString run once in number-hint order
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((trace (js-object :events ""))) (let ((value (js-call globalThis.Math :round (js-object :valueOf (lambda () (put trace :events (str (get trace :events) "v")) (js-object)) :toString (lambda () (put trace :events (str (get trace :events) "s")) "-1.5")) (put trace :events "e")))) (str value ":" (get trace :events)))))

scenarios.given: an object whose numeric conversion callbacks both return objects
scenarios.when: Math.ceil cannot obtain a primitive number
scenarios.then: conversion fails without leaked frames and a later round call succeeds
scenarios.source: (defun run () (Math/ceil (js-object :valueOf (lambda () (js-object)) :toString (lambda () (js-object))))) (defun recover () (Math/round 1.5))

features.name: Live collection callbacks
features.description: Map and Set forEach execute source closures with live mutation, exact arguments and recovery entirely inside collecting zero-import WASM

scenarios.given: a two-entry Map and a callback clearing it during its first visit
scenarios.when: the callback appends a new entry after clearing
scenarios.then: the removed entry is skipped and the appended entry is visited with the same receiver
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((items (new globalThis.Map (js-array (js-array 1 "a") (js-array 2 "b")))) (log (js-array)) (first t)) (js-call items :forEach (lambda (value key receiver) (js-call log :push (js-array value key (eq items receiver))) (when first (setq first false) (js-call items :clear) (js-call items :set 3 "c")))) log))

scenarios.given: a Set and a callback deleting then reinserting the first visited value
scenarios.when: forEach follows the live insertion order
scenarios.then: each callback receives value value Set and the reinserted value is revisited at the end
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((items (new globalThis.Set (js-array 1 2))) (log (js-array)) (first t)) (js-call items :forEach (lambda (value key receiver) (js-call log :push (js-array value key (eq items receiver))) (when first (setq first false) (js-call items :delete value) (js-call items :add value)))) log))

scenarios.given: an empty Map and a noncallable callback
scenarios.when: forEach validates its callback
scenarios.then: validation fails even without entries and a later Set callback succeeds
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-call (new globalThis.Map) :forEach false)) (defun recover () (let ((log (js-array))) (js-call (new globalThis.Set (js-array 7)) :forEach (lambda (value key receiver) (js-call log :push (js-array value key)))) log))

features.name: Sequence concatenation
features.description: Array shallow copying and String concatenation preserve sparse ownership, identity, captured methods and ordered conversions inside collecting zero-import WASM

scenarios.given: a sparse array containing an owned undefined and a shared nested array
scenarios.when: concat copies it twice and the nested array is changed afterwards
scenarios.then: the output is distinct, holes remain absent, undefined remains owned and nested references remain shared
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((items (js-array)) (inner (js-array 1))) (put items :length 4) (put items 1 undefined) (put items 3 inner) (let ((out (js-call items :concat items "tail"))) (put inner 0 7) (js-array (eq items out) (js-length out) (object-has? out 0) (object-has? out 1) (eq (js-nth 3 out) (js-nth 7 out)) (js-nth 3 out) (js-nth 8 out)))))

scenarios.given: two objects with text conversion hooks and an argument with effects
scenarios.when: String.concat evaluates all operands and converts them
scenarios.then: argument effects finish before left-to-right conversion hooks
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((log (js-array)) (first (js-object :toString (lambda () (js-call log :push "first") "1"))) (second (js-object :toString (lambda () (js-call log :push "second") "2")))) (js-array (js-call "a" :concat first (progn (js-call log :push "argument") second)) log)))

scenarios.given: an own concat method that is replaced during argument evaluation
scenarios.when: the call finishes evaluating two arguments
scenarios.then: the original captured function receives both values exactly once
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((items (js-array)) (log (js-array))) (put items :concat (lambda (&rest values) (js-call log :push "captured") values)) (js-array (js-call items :concat (progn (put items :concat false) 1) (progn (js-call log :push "argument") 2)) log)))

features.name: Value identity
features.description: Object.is and Array.isArray preserve exact source value identity and ordinary evaluation without imports or coercion.

scenarios.given: NaN, signed zeros and infinities
scenarios.when: Object.is compares values directly and through an alias
scenarios.then: NaNs compare equal while opposite signed zeros differ
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((same (js* "Object.is"))) (js-array (Object/is (/ 0 0) (/ 0 0)) (Object/is -0.0 0) (funcall same -0.0 -0.0) (Object/is (/ 1 0) (/ 1 0)))))

scenarios.given: objects, arrays and primitive strings with identical contents
scenarios.when: Object.is compares shared and distinct values
scenarios.then: objects retain identity and strings compare by exact UTF-16 contents
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-object)) (b (js-object))) (js-array (Object/is a a) (Object/is a b) (Object/is (js-array) (js-array)) (Object/is "中😀" "中😀") (Object/is 1 "1"))))

scenarios.given: missing arguments and side effects in ignored arguments
scenarios.when: identity predicates are called
scenarios.then: undefined defaults match and every argument runs once
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((trace (js-object :n 0))) (js-array (Object/is) (Object/is 1) (Object/is 1 1 (put trace :n 7)) (Array/isArray (js-array) (put trace :n 9)) (get trace :n))))

scenarios.given: a lexical Object binding with its own is method
scenarios.when: an argument changes that method
scenarios.then: the captured method receives all arguments
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((Object (js-object :is (lambda (&rest args) (js-length args))))) (js-call Object :is 1 2 (put Object :is false))))

features.name: Shallow source object integrity
features.description: Shallow freezing keeps source identity and protects own properties while retaining mutable child objects and collection internal slots, with strict errors and independent recovery.

scenarios.given: an object owns a mutable child
scenarios.when: only the parent is frozen and the child is changed
scenarios.then: the parent keeps identity and only its own properties are frozen
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((child (js-object :value 1)) (parent (js-object :child child)) (result (Object/freeze parent))) (put child :value 2) (js-array (eq parent result) (Object/isFrozen parent) (Object/isFrozen child) (get child :value))))

scenarios.given: a frozen object owns a data property
scenarios.when: a strict assignment writes the same value
scenarios.then: the write fails and a following independent frozen query succeeds
scenarios.source: (defun run () (put (Object/freeze (js-object :x 1)) :x 1)) (defun recover () (Object/isFrozen (Object/freeze (js-object))))

scenarios.given: a frozen Map wrapper contains no entries
scenarios.when: its entries are added and then cleared
scenarios.then: internal entries remain mutable while the wrapper stays frozen
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((m (Object/freeze (new (js* "Map"))))) (js-call m :set "key" 7) (let ((value (js-call m :get "key"))) (js-call m :clear) (js-array value (get m :size) (Object/isFrozen m)))))

scenarios.given: a frozen empty array has an invalid sort comparator
scenarios.when: sort checks that comparator
scenarios.then: the comparator error is preserved even though no item would be written
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-call (Object/freeze (js-array)) :sort false)) (defun recover () (js-length (js-call (Object/freeze (js-array)) :toSorted)))

features.name: Array searching
features.description: includes, indexOf and lastIndexOf execute entirely in collecting zero-import WASM with exact equality, sparse slots and original conversion order.

scenarios.given: NaN and negative zero in an ordinary array
scenarios.when: includes and the strict index methods search those values
scenarios.then: only includes matches NaN and all methods treat both zeros equally
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-array (/ 0 0) -0.0))) (js-array (js-call a :includes (/ 0 0)) (js-call a :indexOf (/ 0 0)) (js-call a :lastIndexOf 0))))

scenarios.given: a sparse array with one explicit undefined position
scenarios.when: all search methods omit their search element
scenarios.then: includes reads holes as undefined while index methods visit only the explicit position
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-array))) (put a :length 4) (put a 2 undefined) (js-array (js-call a :includes) (js-call a :indexOf) (js-call a :lastIndexOf))))

scenarios.given: the same value appears twice
scenarios.when: lastIndexOf either omits fromIndex or explicitly passes undefined
scenarios.then: omission starts at the last slot while undefined converts to zero
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-array 1 2 1))) (js-array (js-call a :lastIndexOf 1) (js-call a :lastIndexOf 1 undefined) (js-call a :indexOf 1 -1.9))))

scenarios.given: a fromIndex callback shrinks the searched array
scenarios.when: includes observes the original length and then reads its removed positions
scenarios.then: a removed position matches undefined and the source shrink remains visible
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((a (js-array 1 2 3)) (from (js-object :valueOf (lambda () (put a :length 0) 0)))) (js-array (js-call a :includes undefined from) (js-length a))))

scenarios.given: an empty array and a fromIndex object unable to convert
scenarios.when: indexOf runs after all argument expressions finish
scenarios.then: it returns minus one without invoking numeric conversion
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-call (js-array) :indexOf nil (js-object :valueOf (lambda () (js-object)) :toString (lambda () (js-object)))))

scenarios.given: an own includes function replaced by an argument effect
scenarios.when: method invocation evaluates the remaining ignored arguments
scenarios.then: the original captured function receives every argument
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((a (js-array))) (put a :includes (lambda (x &rest rest) (str x ":" (js-length rest)))) (js-call a :includes (progn (put a :includes false) "captured") 1 2)))

features.name: Array construction
features.description: Native Array.from and Array.of preserve dense ownership, Unicode iteration, array-like snapshots, live cursors and abrupt closing in independent JS and zero-import collecting WASM.

scenarios.given: undefined and an ordinary object supplied to Array.of
scenarios.when: the result is copied with Array.from
scenarios.then: both arrays own dense slots and retain the original object reference
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((x (js-object)) (a (Array/of undefined x)) (b (Array/from a))) (js-array (js-length a) (object-has? a 0) (undefined? (aref a 0)) (eq (aref b 1) x) (not (eq a b)))))

scenarios.given: a supplementary Unicode character and an isolated high surrogate
scenarios.when: Array.from iterates the string
scenarios.then: the supplementary pair stays together and the isolated code unit survives
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((x (Array/from (str "A😀" (String/fromCharCode 55296))))) (js-array (js-length x) (js-length (aref x 1)) (js-call (aref x 2) :charCodeAt 0))))

scenarios.given: an array-like object with an inherited first item
scenarios.when: its mapper shrinks length and changes a later value
scenarios.then: the original length is retained and subsequent indexed reads observe the change
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let* ((p (js-object :0 "inherited")) (x (js-object :__proto__ p :length 3 :1 "old" :2 "last"))) (Array/from x (lambda (value index) (when (= index 0) (put x :length 1) (put x 1 "new")) value))))

scenarios.given: a Set containing two values
scenarios.when: the mapper deletes the next value and appends another
scenarios.then: live iteration skips the deleted value and visits the appended value with consecutive indices
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((s (new (js* "Set") (js-array "a" "b")))) (Array/from s (lambda (value index &rest rest) (when (= index 0) (js-call s :delete "b") (js-call s :add "c")) (js-array value index (js-length rest))))))

scenarios.given: a source iterator with an own next callback
scenarios.when: the callback overwrites next after the first invocation
scenarios.then: the originally captured callback is used until its done result
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((i (js-call (js-array) :values)) (n 0)) (put i :next (lambda () (setq n (1+ n)) (put i :next false) (js-object :done (> n 2) :value n))) (Array/from i)))

scenarios.given: an iterator whose return callback records closing and itself fails
scenarios.when: the mapper throws an invalid-radix error
scenarios.then: return runs once and the original mapper error survives
scenarios.source: (defconst trace (js-object :closed false)) (defun run () (let ((i (js-call (js-array 1) :values))) (put i :return (lambda () (put trace :closed t) (js-call nil :charAt))) (Array/from i (lambda (value index) (js-call 1 :toString 1))))) (defun recover () (get trace :closed))

features.name: Object own properties
features.description: Own enumerable data properties, key coercion and ordered assignment execute in JS and zero-import WASM while retaining original target identity and failure effects.

scenarios.given: numeric-looking names inserted between ordinary names
scenarios.when: Object.keys enumerates the object
scenarios.then: canonical integer indices precede other names in insertion order
scenarios.source: (defun run () (Object/keys (js-object :z 1 :10 2 :01 3 :2 4 :a 5)))

scenarios.given: a string containing a supplementary Unicode character
scenarios.when: keys and own properties are queried
scenarios.then: indices count UTF16 units and length is own but non-enumerable
scenarios.source: (defun run () (js-array (Object/keys "A😀") (Object/hasOwn "A😀" "length") (Object/hasOwn "A😀" "2") (Object/hasOwn "A😀" "3")))

scenarios.given: a property key object with two conversion hooks
scenarios.when: hasOwn evaluates an extra argument then converts the key
scenarios.then: toString runs once after the argument and valueOf is skipped
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((trace (js-object :n 0))) (let ((found (Object/hasOwn (js-object :x 1) (js-object :toString (lambda () (put trace :n (+ (* (get trace :n) 10) 1)) "x") :valueOf (lambda () (put trace :n 999) "missing")) (put trace :n 2)))) (js-array found (get trace :n)))))

scenarios.given: a sparse array and a target object
scenarios.when: assign copies the array and skips nullish sources
scenarios.then: only owned indices copy and the target keeps its identity
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((target (js-object)) (items (js-array t undefined))) (put items :length 3) (let ((result (Object/assign target nil undefined items))) (js-array (eq target result) (Object/keys result) (Object/hasOwn result "1") (Object/hasOwn result "2")))))

scenarios.given: null-prototype source and target objects with an own __proto__ data name
scenarios.when: assign copies properties
scenarios.then: the name stays ordinary data on the target
scenarios.source: (defun run () (let ((source (js-object :__proto__ nil :x 1)) (target (js-object :__proto__ nil))) (put source :__proto__ "data") (Object/assign target source) (js-array (get target :__proto__) (Object/keys target))))

scenarios.given: an early source and a later source that would make the target its own prototype
scenarios.when: assignment reaches the invalid later property
scenarios.then: the original error is reported and the earlier write remains visible
scenarios.source: (defconst target (js-object)) (defun run () (let ((source (js-object :__proto__ nil))) (put source :__proto__ target) (Object/assign target (js-object :saved 7) source))) (defun recover () (get target :saved))
